name: Krampus
description: The horned Christmas demon who punishes naughty children

debut.title: Alpine folk tradition
debut.era: centuries-old customs of Austria, Bavaria and nearby regions

legend: In the Alps, St. Nicholas doesn't travel alone. On the night of 5 December, Krampusnacht, the eve of St. Nicholas Day, he's joined by Krampus: shaggy, horned, long-tongued and rattling chains and bells. While the saint rewards good children, Krampus swats the naughty with birch switches and, in the scarier tellings, carries them off in a sack. In the 1800s people sent each other Krampus greeting cards, and today towns hold Krampuslauf parades where costumed Krampuses charge through the streets.

myths.explanation: His night is 5 December, Krampusnacht, the eve of St. Nicholas Day.
They work as a team: the saint rewards the good while Krampus deals with the naughty.

myths.claim: Krampus parades are still held today.
myths.explanation: Krampuslauf runs take place every December in Austria, Germany and increasingly around the world.

powers: A sack big enough for a child
legacy: Krampus (2015), a horror comedy by Michael Dougherty
Krampus festivals now held far beyond the Alps
